chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Al-Qasim ibn Al-Rabi', and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, raising it, said:

In the bequest of Al-Mufazzal, I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'No two men separate upon desertion except that one of them incurs disowning and cursing, and sometimes both of them deserve that.'

So Mu'tabb said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is the unjust one, so what is the matter with the oppressed one?' He said: 'Because he does not invite his brother to reconciliation, nor does he overlook his speech.'

I heard my father saying: 'When two dispute, and one overpowers the other, let the oppressed return to his companion until he says to his companion, "Yes, my brother, I am the unjust," until he cuts off the desertion between him and his companion. For indeed Allah, Blessed and High, is a Just Judge who takes for the oppressed from the oppressor.'

key_terms.يَتَغَامَسُ: To overlook or turn a blind eye

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended ethical behavior for the oppressed party in a dispute to end desertion?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the spiritual dynamics of estrangement (hijran), noting that the oppressed party often bears greater responsibility for the separation due to their reluctance to initiate reconciliation or overlook minor faults. The ethical teaching advises the oppressed to take the initiative in mending ties by humbly claiming fault, as Allah is the Just Judge who will rectify the situation. This reflects the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) and *silm* (peace-making) as active virtues rather than passive endurance, aligning with the concept of *adl* (divine justice) where the aggrieved is ultimately vindicated.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Al Qasim Bin Al Rabie, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, raising it, said,

‘In a bequest of Al-Mufazzal, I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘No two men would separate upon the desertion except upon one of the two would Obligate the disowning and the cursing, and sometimes both of them deserve that’.

So Mo’tab said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! This is the unjust one, so what is the matter with the oppressed one?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Because he did not leave his brother to good relations nor did he overlook from his speech.

I<sup>asws</sup> heard my<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When two (people) dispute, so one overpowers the other, so let the oppressed return to his companion until he is saying to his companion, ‘Yes, my brother, I am the unjust’, until he cuts-off the fleeing between him and his companion, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Judges justly. He<sup>azwj</sup> Seizes for the oppressed, from the oppressor’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from al- Qasim ibn al-Rabi’ and certain individuals of our people from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid in a marfu’ manner it is in the advice to al-Mufaddal who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Of the two people who depart each other to abandon and walk out on each other, one is subject to disowning and condemnation or perhaps both of them will face such conditions.’
Mu’attib then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, one is unjust, what about the oppressed?’
The Imam said, ‘It is because he did not ask his brother (in belief) to maintain good brotherly relations and did not ignore his words.

I heard my father saying, “Whenever two people dispute and one of them over power the other, the oppressed should turn to his companion and say to him, ‘O brother (in belief), I am the unjust,”’ so that forsaking and abandonment would not take place among them. Allah, the Most Blessed, the Most High, is the Judge with justice, He judges with justice for the oppressed against the oppressor.’”
